methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates nanomaterial characterization (TEM, HRTEM, XPS, XRD, ICP-AES), paired NF/CAF lines derived from three patient pairs (NF1/CAF1 selected), in vitro ferroptosis readouts (FerroOrange, Liperfluo, intracellular ROS, GPX4/cell viability IC50s with 95% CIs), and a broad in vivo package (CT26 and MC38 syngeneic subcutaneous models with/without coinjected fibroblasts, Apc-KO GEMM, PDX in NOD/SCID, and PDO organoid viability). AS1411 aptamer surface targeting is tested in a six-arm design with laser irradiation. Limitations: the main CAF/NF experiments use a single selected pair (NF1/CAF1), per-group sample sizes are not clearly documented in the provided methods, and statistical analyses appear largely to be triplicate with t-tests/ANOVA without multiplicity correction across many outcomes. Blinding is not described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: A preclinical nanomedicine study spanning cell lines, primary CAFs, GEMM, PDX, and PDO; Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is strong for microsatellite-stable CRC (~85% of mCRC, ICB-refractory), with the TME-remodeling strategy offering a plausible translational path. Iron/copper nanoparticle systems have regulatory precedent (ferumoxytol), supporting potential first-in-human development.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies for the animal arms. Ethics approvals are reported (Peking University Cancer Hospital 2020KT127; IACUC MSE-HouYL-1), housing conditions, tumor-size limits (<=2000 mm^3 or <=10% body weight), and the tumor-volume formula are specified. Dosing, routes, and schedules are detailed. However, sample sizes per group, randomization, blinding, and explicit power calculations are not clearly documented in the provided text. Patient demographic details for fibroblast/organoid/PDX donors are disclosed. Data availability: the abstract mentions a Source Data file for survival/CAF abundance, and GSE17538 is cited for the public bioinformatics analysis, but deposition of new data is not described.

novelty_literature.justification: The work introduces Cu@Fe3O4 core-shell magnetic nanoparticles with AS1411 aptamer surface targeting of CAFs, combining iron-driven ROS/ferroptosis with copper-mediated GPX4 downregulation to preferentially kill CAFs (IC50 ~2.6 uM) over epithelial cells and to remodel the immune TME (CCL3/CXCL12 modulation, DC maturation, CD8+ T activation). While CAF-targeting nanotherapy and ferroptosis are active areas, the dual-metal ferroptosis mechanism combined with PTT/CDT and validated across syngeneic, GEMM, PDX, and PDO platforms is a meaningful extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally well organized with schematic figures (Fig. 1a) and extensive method detail. However, the narrative is dense with acronyms (CDT, PTT, NPs-AS1411), some phrasing is awkward ('ameliorate CAFs'), and there are typos ('NPs-AS411' vs 'NPs-AS1411', '[REDACTED]' placeholders for doses in the Apc-KO section). Methods are comprehensive but long, and per-group sample sizes are not always specified inline.

key_strengths: Comprehensive multi-model validation: syngeneic CT26/MC38 with/without fibroblast coinjection, Apc-KO GEMM, PDX, and PDO organoids
Mechanistically coherent dual-metal ferroptosis induction (Fe-driven ROS + Cu-driven GPX4 downregulation) preferentially targeting CAFs (IC50 ~2.6 uM vs NF ~12.3 uM)
Functional immune remodeling shown via CCL3/CXCL12 ELISA, DC maturation, and CD8+ T cell activation
Use of AS1411 aptamer surface targeting to enhance CAF specificity under NIR irradiation
key_concerns: Primary human CAF/NF experiments rely on a single NF1/CAF1 pair despite three patients isolated; broader biological replicates would strengthen generalizability
Randomization, blinding, and per-group sample sizes for in vivo experiments are not clearly documented
Dosing information is partially redacted in the Apc-KO GEMM experiment, preventing full reproducibility
No multiplicity correction appears to be applied across many comparisons, and pharmacokinetic/biodistribution data are not presented in the excerpt
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rich preclinical nanomedicine study with plausible translational hooks but reporting gaps that warrant major revisions to meet tier-2 standards (Nature Communications oncology / ACS Nano).
